CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's fundamental health is strong: Q1 2026 revenue surged 22% YoY to $17.4B, adjusted EPS of $5.54 beat consensus by 19%, and the company raised both annual and long-term revenue growth targets (low double-digit for 2026; 6-9% CAGR to 2030, up from 5-7%). The record $63B backlog and AI-driven power generation demand provide multi-year revenue visibility. Operating margins held at 18% adjusted despite $710M tariff headwinds, and the company deployed $5.7B to shareholders in Q1 alone. However, valuation is extremely stretched: P/E of 42.7x is at the top of its 365-day range (14-43x), P/B of 23.5x is also at the ceiling, and the stock has tripled in a year. Tariff costs are projected at $2.2-2.4B for full-year 2026, and Resource Industries margins collapsed to 10% from 17%. The near-term catalyst (Q1 earnings beat + raised guidance) has already been priced in with a 10% single-day surge. The fundamental trajectory is genuinely excellent, but the valuation leaves no margin of safety and embeds near-perfect execution.
